title: Advanced Evidence Reasoning Diagnostic
completionNotice: Optional self-test; not part of historical mastery exam scores or an externally verified certification.

tracks.title: Systems and network diagnosis
questions: An owned VM has a correct IP, can reach its DNS resolver, and resolves api.corp.lab. An HTTP request returns connection refused. Which evidence is most useful next?
Replace the resolver because any HTTP error proves faulty DNS
Change the VM address because an IP response rules out service faults
Confirm the intended service is listening on the expected address and port
Name resolution and routing have worked to some extent. A refusal points toward listener or policy/service behavior; inspect the intended endpoint before changing DNS.
A Linux app service says active, but another VM cannot reach TCP 8000. ss -ltn shows 127.0.0.1:8000. Which explanation best fits?
The service listens only on loopback; a second guest needs an approved network-facing listener
The service must have stopped because active status is unreliable
The firewall must be open because a process owns the port
A loopback bind typically excludes external guest clients; confirm expected bind, isolation and firewall before modifying any settings.
A Windows workstation has a default route but cannot resolve an internal domain controller SRV record with its public resolver. Which action best isolates the problem?
Disable the network adapter to trigger automatic domain repair
Run authorized SRV lookup against the documented internal DNS server and compare replies
Reset the domain account password and test again
Testing the same service record with the approved internal resolver distinguishes internal DNS configuration from account or routing faults.
An isolated VM has no default gateway yet can reach another VM on the same internal subnet. How should you interpret this?
Network isolation failed because every VM must have a default route
All TCP applications are necessarily unreachable without a default route
Expected if no external routed connectivity is designed
Connected routes can support local-segment traffic without an external default route. Inspect additional adapters and hypervisor modes before claiming full isolation.

tracks.title: Identity and application authorization
questions: Event 4728 documents a temporary privileged group addition under a ticket that expired 30 minutes ago. Membership still exists. What conclusion is best supported?
The access has outlasted approval; verify activity and arrange authorized removal
The event proves a malicious credential compromise
The approved ticket makes lingering access harmless regardless of policy
The observation establishes expired effective privilege and a review need, but intent requires corroborating evidence.
Two test users authenticate to an owned API. User A receives HTTP 200 for B's private invoice, contrary to policy. What does this demonstrate?
Evidence that live customer data have been stolen previously
An object authorization failure under the synthetic test conditions
A complete bypass of the authentication mechanism
Authentication can succeed while authorization fails. Demonstrate both an allowed owner request and a denied cross-user request after remediation.
An app service identity can read and write every object bucket but requires read-only access to one approved bucket. What change best addresses the observed risk?
Block SSH to the application host and leave the cloud role unchanged
Rotate the service credentials without adjusting the role's permissions
Restrict the service principal's actions and resource scope, then test necessary reads and forbidden writes
Identity privileges and management-network exposure are separate controls. Role scope should match required operations.
A scanner reports an HTTP header absent on one route. What should an assessor do before assigning severity?
Check the route's intended behavior, exploit prerequisites, compensating controls, and reproducible impact
Assume the missing header caused a data breach
Apply the maximum severity because scanning is objective
Configuration observations require context. A missing header by itself does not establish feasible exploitation or organizational impact.

tracks.title: Cloud operations and recovery
questions: A training cloud policy exposes management TCP/22 to all sources; an old vendor exception has expired. There is no evidence of login abuse. How should this be reported?
Mark the risk resolved because application uptime is healthy
Document excessive reachability and propose scoped rollback without claiming compromise
Declare confirmed intrusion because open administrative ports imply exploitation
An exposure finding is valid independently of exploitation. A controlled change should retain approved admin access and verify denied lab-only paths.
Thirty nightly backup jobs show success, but no complete restore has been performed in 14 months. What conclusion is justified?
RTO is guaranteed because the scheduler reports job success
RPO is zero because snapshots run every night
Backup creation is documented; application recovery time and data integrity remain unverified
RTO/RPO require testing recovered application dependencies, data age and actual time to resume service.
An admin-only management VM should reach a disposable test service; a second guest on a restricted segment should not. What is the best verification design?
Test positive access from the owned admin VM and negative access from an owned restricted lab guest
Test public IPs until a deny rule appears
Infer the ACL works from its policy name without testing
Controlled positive and negative lab-only tests show effective access decisions without crossing authorization boundaries.
A configuration diff shows a storage policy changed from one bucket to wildcard access. What is still unknown?
Which resource name was written in the diff
Whether the widened access was exercised or caused data exposure
Whether the configuration text is different from baseline
A diff proves policy drift, not historical use or exploitation. Review activity logs and change approvals with measured confidence.

tracks.title: Professional engagement and retesting
questions: A finding states an owned lab API allowed one unauthorized object read. Which report wording is most defensible?
All data in the system are compromised because a single endpoint failed
The issue is theoretical because only one request was observed
The provided controlled request violated policy; history and external impact remain unverified
A reproducible violation is evidence of the specific flaw while the broader blast radius requires additional authorized investigation.
A remediation ticket says the API added ownership checks. What minimum acceptance evidence supports closing the finding?
The deployed test build permits authorized owner access and denies cross-user access with recorded results
The developer confirmed a source-code change was merged
The staging deployment completed without errors
Both positive and negative behavior tests matter; deployment status and intent cannot substitute for observed access control.
A reviewer sees the student changed their report after a prior review. What is the correct handling?
Delete the original evidence to avoid confusion
Flag the old decision as stale and review the revised supporting evidence
Carry over the prior approval without inspection because the student is the same
Evidence and reviewer decisions must be tied to a stable version or revalidated after material edits.
A fictional incident includes an approved group change, an unrelated DNS outage and a single failed login. What avoids unsupported attribution?
Treat all events within an hour as proof of one attack
Ignore the change ticket because legitimate actions never produce alerts
Create a normalized evidence timeline, distinguish independent causes, and state competing hypotheses
Temporal proximity alone does not establish causality or intent. Cross-source identifiers, authorization records and counterevidence improve conclusions.
